title: Texas Chili with Ancho and Tomatillo

ingredientGroups.title: Beef and chile paste
items: 5 lb chuck roast, trimmed into 1-inch cubes
10 smoked pasilla (ancho) chile pods, deseeded (120 g)

ingredientGroups.title: Vegetables
items: 9–12 garlic cloves, roughly chopped (1 head; 50 g)

ingredientGroups.title: Spices
items: 4 smoked habanero pods, deseeded and ground (3 g)
4 smoked árbol pods, deseeded and ground (2 g)

steps: Stem, seed and remove veins from the dried ancho chiles. Cover with just enough boiling water to submerge and soak 30 minutes, reserving 3 cups soaking water.
Simmer tomatillos in boiling water for 6–8 minutes until soft. Pass the tomatillos and hydrated chiles through a food mill.
Heat a Dutch oven over high heat. Render some fat from the beef trimmings, sear beef in batches and set aside.
Add onion, garlic and poblano and sauté 5 minutes. Add ground habanero, árbol, cumin and salt; stir 30 seconds.
Add chile-tomatillo paste, Worcestershire, beer, chile water and beef concentrate. Bring to a boil and simmer 15 minutes. Blend with an immersion blender if desired.
Return beef and juices, cover and simmer over the lowest heat for 3 hours. Uncover and simmer about 1½ hours more, until meat falls apart.
Serve with cornbread, Fritos, cheddar, onion, cilantro or sour cream. For best flavor refrigerate overnight and reheat the next day.
